| `capture/lab/REDACTIONS.txt` | each file that was cut, shortened, or scrubbed before it was committed, and why |
| `capture/run.py` | rebuilds the summaries from the recordings and checks them, with no network |
| `capture/demos/` | four demos with their recorded runs: an idle suspender, a stateful agent, a tool sandbox, and a failure drill |
| `research/brief.md` | the research brief that the manual was written from |

## The pin

| Agent Substrate | v1.0.0, commit `b34fbee742906494b5eb4f1f36987176bf8770a4`, released 2026-11-05 |

## The recording hosts

| the x86 server guest | a KVM guest with 24 vCPU and 47 GB, with nested KVM |

The clusters are kind clusters with one to three nodes. The kagent and Agent Executor runs used a small open model on CPU, 1 to 2 GB, at 7 to 14 tokens per second. - 34 figures and a cover plate, drawn with the figure kit from the capture files. They animate on the web and show the final frame in print.
- A capture kit in `capture/`, in Python with the standard library only. It runs the real `sbx`, `docker-agent`, and `docker` binaries and writes what they print to `capture/out/`.
- 111 listings. 94 come from `capture/out/`, 11 from `capture/fixtures/`, one from `capture/run.py`, and five from the vendored sources.
- A register of 122 conflicts between the help text, the docs, the repositories, the release notes, the blog posts, the talks, and community threads. Each conflict has the ruling that the manual prints. The register also lists 30 pieces of stale advice, and the migration section prints each one with its current form.
- A ledger of 22 claims from Docker pages and the community, each with a verdict and the capture file behind it.
- 21 behaviors that the recorded run showed and the docs did not say, listed in `capture/README.md`.

## Files

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `manual.json` | the manifest: the pin, the parts, the palette, the sources |
| `front.md`, `sections/` | the text, one file per section |
| `figures/src/` | the figure sources, built to `figures/*.svg` |
| `capture/` | the kit, its fixtures and model cassettes, and its recorded output in `capture/out/` |
| `research/sources/` | the vendored help text, agent file schema, kit spec, docs pages, and release notes, with their licenses |
| `research/*.md` | the plan, the capture plan, and the conflicts register that the sections cite |

## The recording host

The kit was recorded on one Mac with macOS 26.2 on Apple silicon, with these versions:

| Item | Version |
|---|---|
| `sbx` | v0.47.0, revision `0411f50e`, from the Homebrew cask |
| `docker-agent` | v1.149.0, from Homebrew, tag commit `bf4169c` |
| Docker Desktop | 4.94.0, with Engine 29.8.2, buildx v0.37.2, and Compose v5.5.1 |
| Docker Model Runner | `docker model` v1.2.6 on TCP port 12434, with the model `ai/qwen3:4b` |
| sandbox template | `docker/sandbox-templates:shell-docker`, Ubuntu 26.04.1 |
| Python | 3.14 |

The documented default model, `ai/qwen3:latest`, failed twice to pull on that Mac with a digest mismatch. Every agent file therefore names `ai/qwen3:4b`. The kit uses no hosted provider and no API key.

## The capture tiers

`sbx` starts real microVMs from images on Docker Hub, and the agent runs need a model. Thus the kit cannot run offline in CI. It records three tiers:

| Tier | What it needs | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| A | `sbx`, `docker-agent`, and the `docker` client, with no daemon, network, model, or key | versions, root help, `docker-agent doctor`, `toolsets`, `models list`, a dry run, and the legacy Desktop commands (files 00, 01, 16, 29) |
| B | `sbx` signed in, the sandboxd daemon, image pulls from Docker Hub, and HTTPS to `example.com` and `mcp.deepwiki.com` | the sandbox lifecycle, ports, `cp`, templates, `--clone`, policy, secrets, MCP, kits, `env plan`, and skills (files 02 to 15) |
| M | Docker Desktop 4.94.0 with Docker Model Runner on TCP port 12434 and `ai/qwen3:4b` pulled, plus containers, Compose, buildx, and a local registry | agent runs, teams, permissions, sessions, eval, five servers, `share`, Model Runner, Compose, `run --sandbox`, and the v3 kit build (files 17 to 28, 98) |

Tier C needs Cloud Sandboxes, a GitHub token, or a change to `~/.ssh/config`. The kit does not record it, and the sections that need it cite the docs.

Most runs of tier M replay a recorded cassette from `capture/cassettes/` with `--fake`. The eval, three of the servers, one run with an explicit `base_url`, and `run --sandbox` call the model live with `temperature: 0`.

## Run the kit

```bash
cd manuals/docker-sandboxes-101
python3 capture/run.py --check
```

The check captures again into a temporary directory. Then it compares each file with `capture/out/` after it masks the values that change on every run. If `sbx`, `docker-agent`, or `docker` is not installed, the check prints `skipped` with the reason and exits 0. If Docker Model Runner or `ai/qwen3:4b` is absent, the check runs tiers A and B and prints `tier m skipped`.

Run `python3 capture/run.py` to record the files again. Before a full run, sign in with `sbx login`, start Docker Desktop, and pull the model with `docker model pull ai/qwen3:4b`. The kit never signs in and never pulls the model. A full run of the three tiers takes about 17 minutes on an M-series laptop when the images are present.

The kit removes the sandboxes, templates, containers, and secrets that it creates. The global network policy and the pulled images stay. `capture/README.md` lists the prerequisites, the ports, the masks, and each fixture.

## Build and check

From the repository root:

```bash
node manuals/_shared/figkit.js build manuals/docker-sandboxes-101
node site/build-manuals.js
node scripts/audit_manuals.js --manual docker-sandboxes-101
```

On a host with the binaries, the audit runs the full capture check, which needs the sign-in and the model. Set `AIEFS_CAPTURE_SKIP=1` to skip that check. The audit must report `TOTAL 0`. See [manuals/AUTHORING.md](../AUTHORING.md) for the contract.

manuals.markdown:
# LangChain 101

The LangChain Python stack, from the decision to use it at all to an agent that streams, pauses for approval, survives a crash, and leaves a trace. It ends with a service that runs the agent in production. It covers langchain 1.5.0, langchain-core 1.8.0, langgraph 1.2.22, and deepagents 0.7.38. Each decision has a recorded answer. The documentation tells you what each class and parameter does. This manual tells you what happened when we ran it, broke it, and measured it. The web edition is at [aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-langchain-101.html](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-langchain-101.html), and each release of the course attaches the PDF as `aiefs-manual-langchain-101.pdf`.

## What is in it

- 60 sections in 9 parts, then eleven reference sections. Each part opens with a position that our runs support. Part 1 is the decision: the claims beside our runs, a harness shoot-out on a 99-task suite with state checkers, and one agent run. Part 2 goes inside the runtime with traces of real runs. Part 3 covers the install, models, messages, and tools. Part 4 covers `create_agent`, structured output by provider, many tools, middleware, retries, and guardrails. Part 5 covers streaming, checkpointers, durability, stores, and long threads. Part 6 covers LangGraph control flow. Part 7 covers retrieval, MCP, Deep Agents, and LangSmith. Part 8 covers the Agent Server, Agent Chat UI, cost, security (with the file rules and store namespaces of Deep Agents), upgrades, errors, and a failure drill. Part 9 builds one FastAPI service with Postgres, approvals, spans, faults, evals, and several workers. It runs that service on Qwen3 4B, Qwen3 14B, and Claude Haiku 5.5. Five worked agents sit in the parts they apply.
- Each measured number names its machine and the number of runs. Pages that this edition does not measure yet say so, and section 8.8 lists the runs that come in the next edition.
- 94 figures and a cover plate, drawn with the figure kit. The charts read the summary files.
- 287 listings. Each one is cut from an offline capture or from the source at the pinned tag, and the audit checks it line for line.
- Section 1.1 sets each headline claim of the project site beside the result that we measured.
- The reference part holds the `create_agent` parameters, the middleware hooks and classes, the stream modes, the checkpointer and store API, the environment variables, the error strings, a glossary, the register of 32 places where the sources disagree, and the method of the task-suite bench.

## Files

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `manual.json` | the manifest: the pin, the parts, the palette, the sources, the cover plate |
| `front.md`, `sections/` | the text, one file per section |
| `figures/src/` | the figure sources, built to `figures/*.svg` |
| `capture/run.py`, `capture/s_*.py` | the capture kit: it uses no keys and no fake chat model, calls Qwen3 4B on a local Ollama where a scenario needs a model, and writes the files in `capture/out/` that the listings come from |
| `capture/lab/` | 51 experiment folders: `T01-overhead-mac` to `T20-mcp-edges-mac`, `TRC-tracing-mac`, and `T21-langsmith-account-mac`, the real-model runs again in the folders that end in `-x86`, `-x86-real`, and `-mac-real`, the runtime traces in `internals/`, the task-suite bench in `bench/`, the second bench in `bench2/`, the multi-agent runs in `multiagent/`, `last-two-mac/`, the production service of Part 9 in `prodapp-mac/`, and the recorded runs of the five demos. Each folder holds its scripts and raw output, and `capture/lab/README.md` names the rows not to use |
| `capture/lab/summary/` | 48 summary files that the tables and charts read, rebuilt by `capture/labsum.py`. The bench writes its own summary, `capture/lab/bench/summary-mac.json`, with `capture/lab/bench/summarize.py`. `capture/labsum.py` also rebuilds the ten summaries in `capture/lab/prodapp-mac/summary/` and the two run summaries in `capture/lab/prodapp-mac/runs/summary/` |
| `capture/demos/` | five demos with a README and a `run.sh` each: a SQL agent, a retrieval agent, an assistant with memory, a deep agent, and a failure drill |

## The pin

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| langchain | 1.5.0, commit `c2f4036e4c6ca45a8da8a42d8e07a25d2ea48b8f` |
| langchain-core | 1.8.0 |
| langgraph | 1.2.22, with langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.2, langgraph-prebuilt 1.1.2, and langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.2.1 |
| langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite | 3.1.3 |
| deepagents | 0.7.38 |
| langsmith | 0.14.17 |
| Providers | langchain-openai 1.8.0, langchain-anthropic 1.7.10, langchain-ollama 1.1.0 |
| Python | 3.11 or later |
| Verified | 2026-11-14 |

`capture/requirements.txt` holds the exact versions, and section R.8 gives the commit of each repository.

## The recording machines

| Name in the manual | Machine |
|---|---|
| the Mac | an Apple M1 Max laptop with 10 cores and 64 GiB, running Ollama for the local models, the client of the Anthropic API in the bench and in Part 9, the client of the hosted LangSmith API in T21, and the service of Part 9 with PostgreSQL 14 |
| the x86 server guest | a KVM guest with 32 vCPU and 48 GiB, running PostgreSQL 16 and the Agent Server |

The local models are Qwen3 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, and 30B-A3B, and gpt-oss 20B, with `nomic-embed-text` for embeddings, all on Ollama. Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 ran in the task-suite bench, through the Anthropic API, for $0.93. Claude Haiku 5.5 also ran the 20 evals of Part 9, in 64 calls for $0.011, and 60 attacks on the file rules of section 8.4, in 134 calls for $0.021. One run used a new LangSmith account on the free plan, from the Mac, with its ids replaced in the kept files. `capture/lab/README.md` maps each experiment to its machine. Do not compare a number from one machine with a number from another.

## How to read it

Start with the front matter, "How to read this manual". It installs the stack from `capture/requirements.txt` and runs the capture kit once. Read Part 1 once and completely. After that, go to the page that answers your question. When something breaks, start at section 8.6 and the error table in R.6.

## Run the recordings again

The lab recordings need Ollama and Postgres on the Mac and on an x86 server guest, so they cannot run in CI. The scripts of each experiment are in its folder under `capture/lab/`, and section R.10 lists the experiments, the machines, the number of runs, and the method. The five demos in `capture/demos/` each have a README and a `run.sh`.

The captures and the summaries rebuild offline:


The check runs the capture kit again and compares each file in `capture/out/`. It rebuilds every summary from the lab recordings and compares it with the committed file. It prints one `skipped:` line for the lab runs, because it does not start Ollama or Postgres.

manuals.title: Miles 101
manuals.summary: How to run GRPO with Miles on one GPU, choose a model that fits, and check that the run is correct. Every measured line comes from recorded runs on a DGX Spark.
manuals.markdown:
# Miles 101

Reinforcement learning on language models with Miles, from one GRPO run on one GPU to a run you can trust. The manual gets a run going first, then shows how to size it, check that it is correct, and find the cause when it fails. The web edition is at [aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-miles-101.html](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-miles-101.html), and each release of the course attaches the PDF as `aiefs-manual-miles-101.pdf`.

## What is in it

- 34 sections in 8 parts, then five reference sections. Part 1 runs GRPO on one GPU, adds a watchdog, and reads the first ten steps. Part 2 sizes the run, Part 3 gives recipes, and Part 4 covers speed and stability. Part 5 checks a run, Part 6 scales it out, Part 7 debugs it, and Part 8 explains how Miles works inside.
- Every measured line comes from recorded runs on one DGX Spark, and each page says how far the result goes. Pages that one GPU cannot show say what we could only read in the source.
- A cover plate and 18 figures drawn with the figure kit from the runs and the code.
- A capture kit in `capture/` that checks the stored outputs without a GPU.
- A GPU kit in `capture/gpu/` that starts the runs on the DGX Spark.

## Files

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `manual.json` | the manifest: the pin, the parts, the palette, the sources, the cover plate |
| `front.md`, `sections/` | the text, one file per section |
| `figures/src/` | the figure sources, built to `figures/*.svg` |
| `capture/run.py` | the capture kit: `--check` compares the stored outputs, and a plain run rebuilds the summary from the raw run logs |
| `capture/gpu/` | the GPU kit: `miles_grpo.py` starts a run, `watchdog.sh` stops a run whose engine died, `heat-guard.sh` pauses the container when the GPU is too hot, `summarize_miles.py` writes the summary |
| `capture/gpu/out-gb10/`, `capture/gpu/out-l4/` | the logs and checks that the listings are cut from |
| `capture/gpu/summary/miles-gb10-lab.json` | the per-step data and the medians that the tables and charts read |

## The pin

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | `radixark/miles@sha256:c64fa344e3a86715f03c0a1b6a422c474e0035355591a2f6da87bf52a74c52da`, arm64 |
| Miles in the image | main `08752a1283`, 2026-10-15 |
| SGLang in the image | `0.5.22.dev46+g7b6993a` |
| Verified | 2026-10-22 |

## The recording host

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Machine | NVIDIA DGX Spark, one GB10 GPU, 128 GB of memory that the CPU and the GPU share |
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, unless the run name gives another size |
| Data | GSM8K prompts with a binary math reward |
| Trainer | FSDP on one GPU, colocated with the SGLang engine |

The GB10 got hot under hours of load, so a heat guard paused the container at 84 C. Timing numbers come from clean steps that no pause touched, or from runs made before the guard. Two logprob checks ran on an NVIDIA L4 with SGLang 0.5.22 outside the Miles image, and their files say so.

## How to read it

Start with the front matter, "How to read this manual". It gives the five commands of a first run and the five results that change what you do. It also defines three terms: heat guard, pause, and clean step. Run section 1.1 with the watchdog of section 1.2 in a second terminal, because a run whose engine dies does not stop by itself. Use [the lab notes](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-miles-101.html#s-ref-lab-notes) to check a number or to repeat a run.

## Run the kit

```bash
cd manuals/miles-101
python3 capture/run.py --check
```

The check needs no GPU and no network. It replays the watchdog rule on the stored error times of the 16-answer run. It marks the pauses from the pause log and computes every median from the stored steps. Then it checks that each quoted value is still in its file. The raw run logs stay on the DGX Spark. Without them, the check prints `skipped` for the fresh summary and compares only the stored outputs. Set `MILES_LAB_RUNS` to a runs folder that holds `status.txt` to also build the summary again and compare it. `python3 capture/run.py` with that folder replaces the stored summary and the pause log.

## Build and check

From the repository root:

```bash
node manuals/_shared/figkit.js build manuals/miles-101
node site/build-manuals.js
node scripts/audit_manuals.js --manual miles-101
```

The audit runs the capture check. It must report `TOTAL 0`. See [manuals/AUTHORING.md](../AUTHORING.md) for the contract.

rea, the `rea-agents` package at 6.7.0, with the Ghidra 12.1.4 provider, from the first `rea doctor` to an agent that keeps an evidence ledger over MCP. manuals.markdown:
# SGLang 101

SGLang 0.5.22, from one request on a laptop to a fleet of GPUs, with the judgment that the flag list leaves out. The documentation tells you what each of the 535 options of `sglang serve` does. This manual tells you which ones matter, why each feature exists, which defaults assume a machine you do not have, and what we measured when we changed them. The web edition is at [aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-sglang-101.html](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-sglang-101.html), and each release of the course attaches the PDF as `aiefs-manual-sglang-101.pdf`.

## What is in it

- 29 sections in 7 parts, then seven reference sections. Part 1 installs SGLang, checks the server, and follows one request through it. Part 2 follows one request through the three processes and the scheduler. Part 3 is the KV cache. Part 4 makes each forward pass fast, and Part 5 measures a server. Part 6 spreads one model over many GPUs, and Part 7 operates SGLang and closes with SGLang as the rollout engine of Miles.
- Every section tells one story: the cost, the obvious fix and why it fails, what SGLang does, what to measure, our position on the default, and a real incident with its link.
- Every number carries one of four labels: we measured, the code, a field report from engineers outside the SGLang team, or a team or vendor claim.
- A cover plate, 63 figures drawn with the figure kit from the captures and the code, and charts plotted from the GPU runs.
- A capture kit in `capture/` that starts the real server on Apple silicon through MLX, sends requests, runs the official benchmark, and writes what it sees to `capture/out/`.
- A GPU kit in `capture/gpu/` that runs eight server configurations and three-seed benchmark sweeps on one NVIDIA GPU, with the GPU clock and temperature of every run.

## Files

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `manual.json` | the manifest: the pin, the parts, the palette, the sources, the cover plate |
| `front.md`, `sections/` | the text, one file per section |
| `figures/src/` | the figure sources, built to `figures/*.svg` |
| `capture/` | the kit and its recorded output in `capture/out/` |
| `capture/gpu/` | the GPU kit, its output in `capture/gpu/out-gb10/`, and the chart data in `capture/gpu/summary/` |

## The pin

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| SGLang | 0.5.22, tag `v0.5.22`, commit `baa9befa381511cd4d56f83980951e5a45fffc6d`, tagged 2026-10-13 |
| Miles | v0.1.2, commit `a22fd824`, for section 7.2 only |
| Verified | 2026-10-16 |

## The recording host

| Item | Version |
|---|---|
| Host | macOS 26.2 on Apple silicon, arm64 |
| SGLang | 0.5.22 from the tag with the `srt_mps` extra |
| Frameworks | PyTorch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.4, Python 3.12.12 |
| Model | `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit` |

The GPU runs were recorded on an NVIDIA DGX Spark with one GB10 (compute capability 12.1, aarch64), SGLang 0.5.22 from PyPI, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, and CUDA 13.0, with `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` and its FP8 checkpoint. `capture/README.md` describes how to run the GPU kit.

## Run the kit

```bash
cd manuals/sglang-101
python3 capture/run.py --check
```

Run it with the Python of the SGLang environment. The check starts the same four servers again, records into a temporary directory, and compares the facts that must not change: the text at temperature 0, token and cached-token counts, request counts, the KV bytes per token, the metric names, and the option list. Without SGLang 0.5.22 and MLX on Apple silicon, the check prints `skipped` with the reason and exits 0. A full run takes 20 to 25 minutes, and `capture/README.md` lists every file it writes.

manuals.summary: How to install vLLM, fit a model on your GPU, tune it for your traffic, and fix it from a symptom. Measured on an NVIDIA L4 and a DGX Spark with vLLM 0.31.0.

# vLLM 101

vLLM 0.31.0, from your first server to a deployment you can size, tune, and debug, with a measured answer for each decision. The documentation tells you what each flag does. This manual tells you which flags matter for your GPU and your traffic, and what happened when we changed them. The web edition is at [aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-vllm-101.html](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-vllm-101.html), and each release of the course attaches the PDF as `aiefs-manual-vllm-101.pdf`.

## What is in it

- 44 sections in 8 parts, then eight reference sections. Parts 1 to 7 follow the order of your work. You start a server, size it, tune it for your traffic, and add speed features. Then you measure it, scale it out, and operate and debug it. Part 8 explains how vLLM works inside, for when a default surprises you.
- Each page answers one question and ends with a check that proves the change worked.
- Each measured number names its machine, its date, its clock, and its seed count. Pages that we could not measure say so.
- A cover plate and 26 figures drawn with the figure kit, with charts plotted from the GPU runs.
- A reference part with the flag table, the metrics, and an index of the GitHub issues the manual cites. It also has the version pins, a glossary, the sources, and the lab notes with the full tables.

## Files

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `manual.json` | the manifest: the pin, the parts, the palette, the sources, the cover plate |
| `front.md`, `sections/` | the text, one file per section |
| `figures/src/` | the figure sources, built to `figures/*.svg` |
| `capture/gpu/summary/` | the summaries of the GPU sweeps that the tables and charts read: `l4.json`, `l4-gpu1.json`, `gb10.json` |
| `capture/gpu/out-l4/`, `capture/gpu/out-gb10/` | the server logs and the live checks that the listings are cut from |
| `capture/gpu/incidents/` | the logs of the failures that the troubleshooting pages show |

## The recording hosts

| Item | NVIDIA L4 | DGX Spark |
|---|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA L4, compute capability 8.9, 24 GB | NVIDIA GB10, compute capability 12.1, 128 GB of unified memory |
| CPU architecture | x86_64 | aarch64 |
| Driver | 615.71.09 | 580.159.03 |
| How vLLM ran | the pip wheel in a virtual environment | the image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` |
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, its FP8 checkpoint, and the EAGLE3 draft `Tengyunw/qwen3_8b_eagle3` | `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` |

The L4 clock changed with its temperature and with other work on the node, so the front matter splits the L4 runs into four sessions. Compare two L4 numbers only inside one session.

## How to read it

Start with the front matter, "How to read this manual". It gives five commands that start a server, then the order of the parts and the four L4 sessions. Read Part 1 once and completely. After that, go to the page that answers your question. Use [the lab notes](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-vllm-101.html#s-ref-lab-notes) to check a number or to repeat a run.

## Run the sweeps again

The GPU runs come from the sweep tool of SGLang 101, `manuals/sglang-101/capture/gpu/sweep.py`. It has a profile for each machine and a vLLM configuration for each table. It needs an NVIDIA GPU, vLLM 0.31.0, and the SGLang 0.5.22 benchmark client. [The lab notes](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-vllm-101.html#s-ref-lab-notes) give the seeds, the server settings, the pool sizes, and the clock rule. [The benchmark page](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-vllm-101.html#s-benchmark-your-server-in-15-minutes) prints the full client command.

This manual has no offline capture check. The stored logs and summaries in `capture/gpu/` are the record, and the audit checks every listing against them.

## Build and check

From the repository root:

```bash
node manuals/_shared/figkit.js build manuals/vllm-101
node site/build-manuals.js
node scripts/audit_manuals.js --manual vllm-101
```

The audit must report `TOTAL 0`. See [manuals/AUTHORING.md](../AUTHORING.md) for the contract.
